title: Python tooling is navigable by subsystem
goal: An agent changing one subsystem of _tools finds its code, its contracts and its tests by file name without loading unrelated subsystems: the large test files and kbgit.py and benchmarks.py are split along their change boundaries into flat-prefixed modules behind unchanged CLIs, a written standard and a test hold the layout, and a before-and-after navigation benchmark says whether splitting further pays
notes: Layout: flat prefixes in _tools/ (ql_, kg_, bench_, test_ql_, test_kb_), as querylog.py over ql_*.py already does; no packages, no new runtime dependency, public CLI paths unchanged. Split by change boundaries, never by size; a story may end in a keep-whole verdict. Out of scope here: splitting kbfacts.py and factdiff.py (the co-change report gives them verdicts for a later sprint); backlog.py and kbgit.py were split in SP-tpulmoxh, the item writers kept whole until ST-leqf5onn, dataclass conversions, renumbering exit codes. ST-3p6lizv4 “A generated map of _tools symbols and tests replaces reading their source” in SP-mqjeanq3 is the other half of the same aim. Shared-component lessons from the sessions that worked _tools: a split moves tests with their code and keeps test names, since item checks select by -k; patched names move with the code; shared fixtures move first; a prefixed module never imports its facade; a moved module needs its map row, tools-map and docs in the same commit; the CLI's parser block and the per-subcommand tools.md rows and backlog.md sections are what sessions collide on, so each module owns its own. ST-d3uyx3pv and ST-pkprc4oy carry the detail;
